title: Tenant Host Identity Resolution Semantic Contract
description: Draft semantic contract for resolving request host identity to tenant context before authentication callback and session handling. The first implementation slice requires active custom-domain ownership to resolve only to the owning tenant and all inactive, unknown, or other-tenant host cases to fail closed.
aiGuidance: Host identity resolution is a semantic prerequisite for tenant-scoped authentication. Do not treat custom-domain source evidence as live-provider login proof.

stateModel.description: Host resolution state covers platform host, slug tenant host, active custom tenant host, verified-but-inactive custom host, custom-domain conflict, reserved host, invalid host, and unknown host fail-closed outcome.

permissions.description: Host resolution happens before authenticated user permissions exist; it produces tenant context rather than authorizing user action.

validation.description: Custom host origin must select the correct tenant realm and callback URL only for active owned domains, and must not treat verified-but-inactive, unknown, or other-tenant domains as tenant context. Mock or local proof is not live IdP readiness.

errorModel.description: Unknown, inactive, disabled, invalid, reserved, or other-tenant host identity fails closed and must not create an authenticated tenant context or callback origin.

auditModel.description: The first slice requires rejected domain conflict and denied host-resolution outcomes to remain audit-visible without leaking ownership tokens. Detailed host-resolution audit taxonomy remains a later expansion.

uiSemanticDefinition.description: Host identity resolution is request-context semantics, not a direct UI surface in the first slice.
